To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) astrocytes respond to neuronal activity with elevations in intracytoplasmic calcium; 2) the calcium elevations in astrocytes occur in response to the release of the neurotransmitter glutamate; 3) the calcium signals in astrocytes are propagated to other astrocytes and to blood vessels; 4) astrocytic calcium signals can modulate neuronal activity and synaptic transmission; 5) astrocyte-neuron signaling can occur via glutamate release
